headline: LITHIUM PLUNGES TO 10-MONTH LOW — 14% WEEKLY COLLAPSE AS BATTERY DEMAND FEARS MOUNT
snippet: Chinese lithium carbonate prices extended their slump through October 15, capping a 14% weekly decline that pushed benchmark prices to a near 10-month low as mounting battery demand concerns weigh on the sector. Bloomberg reports that weaker-than-expected Q3 orders from major Chinese battery manufacturers and EV adoption slowdown fears in key European markets are driving the latest leg down, even as CATL's Jianxiawo mine restart adds supply-side pressure.

headline: HARVARD BELFER: CHINA URANIUM ENRICHMENT ON PACE FOR 15.4M SWU BY YEAR-END — CAPACITY EXCEEDS CIVILIAN NEEDS
snippet: A Harvard Belfer Center analysis by Hui Zhang finds China's uranium enrichment capacity is on track to reach approximately 15.4 million SWU per year by end-2026 — more than double its 2020 level — and concludes the expansion significantly exceeds projected civilian power requirements, suggesting it may also support an accelerating nuclear weapons buildup. The analysis adds a geopolitical dimension to the uranium investment thesis: a China targeting 110 GWe of nuclear capacity by 2030 is a structural demand driver, while simultaneously expanding enrichment at a pace that rivals Western suppliers.

headline: PRECIOUS METALS RECOVER FOR SECOND DAY — SILVER UP 0.8% TO $57.91, GOLD ABOVE $4,180 AHEAD OF FOMC
snippet: Silver rose 0.8% to $57.91 per ounce on October 16 in the second consecutive recovery session after the October 14 CPI-driven selloff that briefly dragged silver near $56. COMEX gold held above $4,180, with bulls targeting the $4,230 area and attention now fully focused on the October 27-28 FOMC meeting as the next key catalyst for precious metals direction.

headline: ENERGYX SIGNS BINDING 10-YEAR DEAL WITH TRAFIGURA — 100,000 TONNES BATTERY-GRADE LITHIUM, $2B+ VALUE
snippet: EnergyX and Trafigura signed a binding 10-year take-or-pay lithium offtake agreement on October 12-13, with Trafigura securing 100,000 tonnes of battery-grade lithium carbonate and hydroxide — EnergyX's first major commercial supply agreement. Based on current market prices near $20,000 per tonne, the deal represents more than $2 billion in revenues over its term, with supply targeted from EnergyX's Project Black Giant in Chile and Project Lonestar in Texas, with first production planned for 2028.

headline: JEFFERIES RATES G MINING BUY — 62% OF 2026 GOLD PRODUCTION SET TO FALL IN SECOND HALF
snippet: Jefferies reaffirmed its Buy rating on G Mining Ventures (TSX: GMIN), citing a strongly back-end weighted 2026 production profile: approximately 62% of the company's 160,000-190,000 ounce guidance is expected to be delivered in the second half as Tocantinzinho accesses higher-grade Phase 2 mineralization. The bank notes near-term revenue dilution from the Franco-Nevada streaming deal but says the setup remains compelling with gold above $4,000/oz and Q3 production already up 16% quarter-on-quarter.

headline: HOCHSCHILD HOLDS 2026 GUIDANCE AMID $58 SILVER, $4,000 GOLD — LONDON-LISTED MINER LEVERAGED TO METALS REBOUND
snippet: Hochschild Mining (LON: HOC), the London-listed silver-gold producer operating in Peru and Chile, confirmed its 2026 production outlook, reaffirming that it remains on track to meet full-year guidance despite ongoing cost pressures. With silver holding near $58/oz and gold above $4,000, Hochschild's Peru and Chilean operations sit in a highly leveraged position on current precious metals prices — one of the few London-listed ways to get direct silver miner exposure.

headline: MIDLAND EXPLORATION HITS NEW GOLD BOULDERS AT CANIAPISC — PHASE 1 RESULTS CONFIRM UP-ICE TARGETS, JAMES BAY
snippet: Midland Exploration (TSXV: MD) identified new gold-bearing boulders during the first phase of its 2026 exploration program at the Caniapisc Au project in Quebec's James Bay region, building on discoveries that returned up to 24.5 g/t Au in 2025 boulder grab samples. The company is tracking the source of the glacially transported gold boulders to up-ice IP anomalies, with a planned drill program intended to test the subsurface targets and evaluate whether Caniapisc hosts a significant bedrock system.

headline: Ur-Energy: $50-55/LB ALL-IN COST VS $97/LB URANIUM TERM PRICE — WIDEST PRODUCER MARGIN IN DECADES
snippet: Ur-Energy outlined its production economics at the Mining Forum Americas 2026, confirming all-in operating costs of $50-55 per pound against the current long-term uranium contract price of $96.50/lb — a spread of $41-47 per pound that represents one of the widest producer margins in the sector's history. The company is expanding its Shirley Basin and Lucky Lake operations to capitalize on US utility demand for domestic, non-Russian, non-Kazakh supply, positioning itself ahead of the looming 2027 contract renewal cycle.

headline: ANALYST: LITHIUM DOWNTURN NOT OVER — 2027 OVERSUPPLY RISK AS MINE RESTARTS OUTPACE EV DEMAND
snippet: An Investing.com analysis argues the lithium market's downturn is far from complete, citing Rothschild & Co Redburn projections of a renewed supply surplus in 2027 as Chinese mine restarts and global expansions are expected to outpace EV demand growth. With Chinese benchmark carbonate prices hitting 10-month lows this week near the $18,000/tonne marginal cost floor for Chinese lepidolite producers, the piece frames current prices as a support level — not a bottom — and warns that a break below $18,000 could trigger sector-wide project deferrals.

headline: 5 GOLD MINING STOCKS TO WATCH AS SECTOR TRAILS BULLION — ANGLOGOLD +257% YTD MASKS DEEP DIVERGENCE
snippet: A Yahoo Finance analysis spotlights five gold mining stocks positioned for outperformance amid ongoing sector pressures, with the study noting that AngloGold Ashanti's 257% year-to-date gain masks deep divergence in how gold miners have performed relative to the bullion price in 2026. The piece highlights companies with strong balance sheets, near-term operational catalysts, and gold price leverage as the preferred framework for identifying mining equity opportunities in a market where the sector still trades at a 22% discount to its 20-year forward earnings average.
